text_blocks.snippet: Jardiance (empagliflozin) can cause a range of common and serious side effects because it works by helping your kidneys remove excess sugar through your urine.

list.snippet: Urinary tract infections (UTIs): Symptoms include burning, urgency, frequency, and cloudy or bloody urine.
Genital yeast infections: These can affect both women (itching, burning, thick white discharge) and men (redness, itching, swelling, or pain around the penis).
Increased urination: You may need to pee more often or in larger amounts than usual.
Other mild effects: Upper respiratory tract infections, increased thirst, nausea, joint pain, and mild weight loss.
Dehydration and low blood pressure: Loss of water and salt can cause dizziness, lightheadedness, or feeling faint—especially when standing up.

Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA): A life-threatening buildup of acid in the blood, which can happen even if your blood sugar is not very high. Symptoms include nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, tiredness, trouble breathing, and fruity-smelling breath.
Severe urinary tract or kidney infections: Such as pyelonephritis or urosepsis, marked by high fever, chills, and lower back or side pain.

Necrotizing fasciitis (Fournier's gangrene): A rare but life-threatening bacterial infection of the tissue under the skin in the perineum (area between the genitals and anus) causing severe pain, redness, and swelling.
Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia): More likely if you take Jardiance alongside other diabetes medications like insulin or sulfonylureas.
Lower limb amputations: An increased risk has been observed, particularly in patients with a history of amputation, peripheral vascular disease, or foot ulcers.
Severe allergic reactions: Symptoms include hives and swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, leading to trouble swallowing or breathing.

text_blocks.snippet: You can review full safety details directly through the Jardiance Official Patient Resource or the Mayo Clinic Drug Guide.
